answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks, so influence must pass through supported paths rather than a single claim. A sybil cluster joined to the honest graph by a sparse external cut has low conductance; under a normalized walk seeded outside the cluster, the cut bounds the probability of entering it and therefore its aggregate voting weight. Min-cut transitivity limits indirect amplification: unlike a mesa, orchard, or dune, the cluster cannot gain weight merely by adding internal identities.
